answer: Latency-weighted admission curve. Each new identity pays a registration cost proportional to the square of identities admitted to its sponsor in the last epoch, so early identities are cheap and late ones expensive. A saffron marker tags sponsor lineage for auditing. Attackers must spread across many sponsors or pay steep marginal costs. The lantern audit log exposes clusters; fable aside, cost per sybil rises superlinearly, capping swarm size.
